title: Oscar and the Hollow
premise: Zephyrine Voss, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who fell silent a decade ago, has survived by staying in the Hollow—a valley where magic cannot follow and the god's enemies cannot see. When a dying cartographer presses her a map of doors out of Vael, a country that was erased from the world's memory, she learns the valley's silence is not sanctuary but a slow devouring: the Hollow eats memories, and hers are nearly gone. Pursued by the Chorus, agents of the power that unmade Vael, she must follow the map to the last true door while deciding whether loyalty to her silent god—or the truth of what he did to deserve his silence—matters more than survival. In the end she opens the door not to escape but to speak Vael's name aloud, restoring it at the cost of her own remembered life; the novel closes with Zephyrine walking out of the valley as a stranger to herself, carrying only the map and a new, small vow.
about_author: Vesper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maps of places that no longer appear on any chart. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, divine, and personal—from a drafty house full of unlabeled keys.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She takes a routine escort job through the Hollow, establishing the valley's rules: no magic, fading memories, a silent god called the Warden. She forgets her mother's face on the road home. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath competent routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A bleeding stranger stumbles into the ferry town, pursued by something unseen. He presses a leather map case into her hands and dies whispering that 'the door still opens for the named.' Emotional beat: unwilling inheritance, guilt at taking nothing and everything.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, brief interlude from the map itself (annotated marginalia). The map depicts Vael—a country she has never heard of—with seven marked doors, one inside the Hollow. Her own name is written on the map in her handwriting she doesn't remember. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: The Oath That Answers Nothing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She prays at the Warden's empty shrine seeking permission; the silence feels different now, deliberate. Her mercenary company notices her distraction. Flashback fragments show the day the god went quiet. Emotional beat: faith curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Chorus Arrives
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Zephyrine and Ilex, a Chorus agent. Polite, terrifying strangers come asking after a dead cartographer, singing questions in harmony. Zephyrine lies well—but they leave a mark on her doorframe that hums. Emotional beat: hunted without yet being chased.

chapters.title: The Company Votes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Her captain, Brannoc, demands she hand over the map or leave the company; loyalty vs. truth fractures old friendships. Her closest friend Sefa covers for her one last time. Zephyrine leaves in the night. Emotional beat: the cost of choosing a path.

chapters.title: First Door: Sealed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At the first marked door, a drowned chapel, she finds it fused shut—and evidence someone tried recently. A Chorus scout ambushes her; she survives by cunning, not skill, and takes his tuning fork. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ilex's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Inside the Chorus, we learn they erase countries by unsinging their names, and Ilex begins questioning an order to burn a village of 'remnant' survivors. His handler notices hesitation. Emotional beat: conscience as liability.

chapters.title: The Memory Merchant
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In a border slum she trades a year of memory to a merchant for translation of the map's script: the final door requires 'a name freely given back.' She chooses which memory to sell—and keeps the wrong one. Emotional beat: sacrifice miscalculated.

chapters.title: Sefa's Letter
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A smuggled letter reveals the Chorus took Sefa hostage to draw Zephyrine out, and that Brannoc is cooperating under duress. Zephyrine must decide whether rescue serves the mission or dooms it. Emotional beat: love as leverage.

chapters.title: The Hollow Remembers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Returning deep into the valley, she finds the second door hidden beneath the Warden's shrine—the god's silence was a seal, holding the door closed from within. The valley isn't hiding her; it's imprisoning something. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Quiet God
chapters.summary: Interleaved POV: the Warden's fragmented consciousness speaks for the first time in ten years. He sealed himself in to stop the Chorus using him as a key—he was Vael's last god, and he surrendered his name to save it. Emotional beat: pity replacing abandonment.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She trades herself to the Chorus for Sefa's release, walking into their camp singing their own harmonies back at them. Ilex is ordered to interrogate her. Emotional beat: courage braided with recklessness.

chapters.title: Two Prisoners
chapters.summary: Alternating Zephyrine/Ilex POV. Interrogation becomes conversation; Ilex confesses he once helped unsing a country and remembers nothing of it—including whether he loved anyone there. Zephyrine offers him the map's truth. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Chorus's True Purpose
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. He discovers the Chorus isn't destroying Vael out of malice—they are feeding erased names to something older beneath their citadel, and Vael is merely the latest course. Emotional beat: horror at scale, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Escape Through Unsung Country
chapters.summary: Zephyrine, Ilex, and freed Sefa flee across land where Vael's erasure left wounds in reality—roads ending mid-stride, rivers flowing uphill toward absence. Sefa begins forgetting Zephyrine in real time. Emotional beat: grief accelerating.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Choice
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The company, shamed, intercepts the Chorus pursuit column at a bridge and holds it at terrible cost so the fugitives can reach the citadel's back way. Brannoc dies buying hours. Emotional beat: redemption paid in full.

chapters.title: Beneath the Citadel
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the vault where stolen names are kept, she confronts the thing that eats countries: a hollow vastness wearing the shapes of everyone it has consumed. It offers her back every memory she's lost if she surrenders the map. Emotional beat: temptation at its most intimate.

chapters.title: The Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: Climax, Zephyrine's POV. She realizes the seventh door is the Warden himself, and the price of opening it is a name given back willingly. She gives the Warden her name—not her life—to complete his sacrifice, and the door opens. The Hollow begins to sing. Emotional beat: self-annihilation as the purest act of will.

chapters.title: Vael, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. As Zephyrine speaks Vael's name through the open door, the country reasserts itself across the world; the Chorus collapses as its master starves; Ilex suddenly remembers a sister, a garden, a debt. The Warden, restored, weeps. Emotional beat: catharsis, restoration with wounds intact.

chapters.title: Stranger to Herself
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The price holds: everyone who ever knew her remembers her differently or not at all; Sefa looks at her with polite blankness. Zephyrine walks out of the restored Vael carrying the map and nothing else of her past. Emotional beat: bittersweet freedom, identity as choice rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: A New Small Vow
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue tone. On a road outside the world's memory, she meets travelers who don't know her and introduces herself with a name she invents on the spot—then hears the Warden's voice, faint and warm, approve it. She turns toward the horizon. Emotional beat: quiet hope, story closed but life open.
